name: RTC Pipe Engine
description: Ported from RTCV's real RTC_PipeEngine.GenerateUnit: takes the Precision-byte value at one source address and copies it, unmodified, into a run of random destination addresses — the classic "pipe one value everywhere" broadcast effect RTCV is known for. The original continuously re-reads a live, possibly cross-domain source every tick; this snapshots the source once and pipes that same value into every destination the run picks.
author: Ported from RTCV (RTC_PipeEngine.cs) for RTCFS4A

parameters.label: Precision (bytes)
parameters.description: Size of the value copied from source to each destination.

parameters.label: Source Byte
parameters.description: -1 = pick one random source address for this whole run. 0 or above uses that exact byte offset — handy for deliberately broadcasting a specific spot you already know is interesting.

parameters.label: Blast Count
parameters.description: How many destinations get the source value piped into them. Use the number box next to the slider for exact values.

parameters.label: Alignment
parameters.description: Sub-offset added after rounding down to Precision, applied to both the source and every destination address, exactly as in the original.

parameters.label: Start Byte
parameters.description: -1 = auto (right after Header Size below). Restricts where both the random source (if Source Byte is -1) and destinations can land.

parameters.label: Header Size
parameters.description: Bytes to leave alone at the start of the file when Start Byte is -1. 16 for .nes/.fds, 512 for headered .smc, 0 for a headerless ROM.

parameters.label: Seed
parameters.description: -1 = random (a fresh seed every run, still recorded for Export Config to reproduce it later). Any value 0 or above is used as a fixed seed instead.

parameters.label: Last Seed Used
parameters.description: Internal bookkeeping: the actual seed the most recent run used, recorded here (not in Seed itself) so Export Config can reproduce it without flipping Seed out of auto mode.
